title: In This Town, Kids Are The Bosses

publish.title: Kids Are The BOSSES In This Town #shorts
publish.description: In this town, kids run every company and adults need permission for everything, until a seven-year-old orders a tower made of slides. What would you build if you were the boss?
publish.caption: In this town, kids are the bosses 👷🛝

scenes.line: In this town, kids are the *bosses*. Adults just work here.
scenes.title: IN THIS TOWN...

scenes.line: You get your first company at age *six*.
My little brother Max runs a construction *site*.
He is seven. He has forty *employees*.
Adults need permission for *everything*. Even lunch.
Max said *no*. He wanted the pizza first.
I was twelve. I had no company. *Embarrassing*.
So Max hired me. As his *assistant*.
My first job: tell the builders Max's new *idea*.
A tower. One hundred floors. Made of *slides*.
The builders said slides are not *walls*, sir.
Max said: *more* slides.
Then he added a pool. On the *roof*. Full of juice.
And an elevator that only goes *sideways*.
Nobody could say no. He was the *boss*.
So they built it. Exactly as *ordered*.
It was the ugliest building in *history*.
It leaned left. It leaked juice. It made a *noise*.
Max walked in for the grand *opening*.
And the whole tower started to *wobble*.
Every adult knew how to fix it. Nobody *moved*.
They were waiting for *permission*.
Max looked at me. For once, he had no *idea*.
So I broke the biggest rule in *town*.
I asked the adults: what would *you* do?
Turns out they had forty years of *ideas*.
Real walls. Real floors. And they kept *one* slide.
The tower stopped wobbling. The town *cheered*.
Max made a new rule that day. Bosses *listen* first.
He even gave the builders a *trophy*. Best Team Ever.
And me? I finally started my own *company*.
We do one thing. We ask people what they *think*.
Business is great. Max is my first *customer*.
He still wants more *slides*, though.
